Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speakerâ€™s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. DRAFT MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  October 23, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 6:30 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEM(S)

CLOSED SESSION (6:30 P.M. - 7:30 P.M.)

This time has been set aside for the City Council to meet in a closed session to discuss the matters
listed below pursuant to Government Code §54957. The Mayor or City Attorney will give an
additional oral report regarding the closed session.

PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
Government Code §54957
Title: City Attorney

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

At the conclusion of the Closed Session, the Council may continue any item listed on the closed
session agenda to the Open Session agenda for discussion or to take formal action as it may deem
appropriate.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL (6:30 PM)

PRESENT:  Mayor Bird, Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, Councilmember Humphrey,
  Councilmember Perkins, Councilmember Rea
ABSENT:

 Mr. Charles Daniel- 1368 Via Cornnel discussed peacocks becoming so predominating in his
area. They keep you awake at night. Stated that if you go away for a couple of days there is
droppping all over the lawn, porch and roof, all around. He counted 11 peacocks in the area.
There's peacocks there every day. It's a nusiance. We've had support by the City before. They put
out the catchers. However the catchers are not effective. They have put grapes out for the
Peacocks.. they eat the grapes but they will not go in the catcher. The peacock are most active early
in the morning around 7am and the people that man the traps do not get there until 9am. The
peacocks have already come and gone. In the afternoon the City closes the traps down to avoid
the peacocks from being trapped overnight and getting eaten by racoons. Keep the peacock count
down to the limit. Mr. Daniel has had about 16 peacock in his yard at one time. Eat his flowers.
Mayor asked how long trap has been out on his property. The trap was put out in July. Mayor
assured Mr. Daniel that the staff will deal with it.

Bobbi Patton- 1409 Via Davlos also discussed the peafowl. Stated that she knows that is not a
favorite topic of the City and that residents are polarized to either side of the issue . She is neither a
lover or hater. However she has lost patiences this year, the numbers are out of control. The
neighbors on her street have counted between 17 to22 birds at one time. She has personally had 17
on her front lawn at one time. She also counted 22 at the corner house at one time in the past two
weeks. This year is every bit as bad as the year that lead to the most recent lawsuit in the early
2000's. Big round up then. Think that needs to happen again. Her understanding of the peafowl
management program is that there are to be 42 birds in the City. 21 in the Malaga Cove area and 21
in Espinosa Circle. Our street is in neither of those designated areas and we have more than that in
our street alone. Has been told by the Streets & Parks Department, Police Department, and the City
Manager that they are only authorized to deploy one trap at a time. The trap is only active between
8 am to 3 pm and birds are most active to 6-8am and 4-7pm, so the trap is not effective. The traap
near her property has only caught two bird in the past month. Four neighbors have taken desperate
measures- cutting down pine tree to try to rob the birds of nesting areas on their properties. Birds
eat and trample flowers and vegetable garden. They soil properties with their dropping, break roof
tiles, and keep residents awake at night. She has personally picked up more dropping from the birds
than from her large dog. Begging the City to live up to the peafowl management program. Taking
a count of the birds in the desinated area only is not taking a true census of the birds and deploying
one trap at a time for limited hours, that do not correspond to the peafowl habits is not a solution.
She would hate to see the City spend more money defending yet another lawsuit which will
probably end up with the same result as the past two lawsuits. Please, do something different than
what is being done to control the out control population. Thanks Council.

Sarah Neuman- 1425 Via Davalos. Prior to that she lived at 1505 Via Historisis, she has been a
resident of Palos Verdes Estates for 32 year resident. City has never had as many peacocks as it
does now. Concerned about our health and noise. Asks the Council to do something proactive to
diminish the population. Thank you.

Carol Hannemann- 1420 Via Davalos. Would like to urge the City to adopt stronger measure for
trapping peafowl. Would like more traps like the traps that Pete Tepus has made and she would like
suggest catcher nets from air guns. Get the City of RPV to trap as well. Birds are coming

are doing now. Surely the City can come up with the finds to deal with this issue now before the

to vet. No sense to have another lawsuit. Council should let everyone know that the Peacock
ouside the designated areas would be trapped. More solutions and trapping. Thank you.

Mayor- Brown Act law will not let us debate the topic tonight. It sounds like the peacocks are
migrating. Staff will take a look into this issue and report back to council with regard to hours of
trapping. Invite members of the public to hold Council accountable that you find that the problem is

12.  City Manager's Report

Reported that after two weeks the City has over 90 persons enrolled in the PV PACE Cars Pledge
Program. The City has distrubuted that many stickers. Out of that 90- 33 of those were distributed
by the Police Department as part of a warning citation- those drivers received a warning citation
along with a sticker and information about the program- urging them to enroll in it. Out of the
streets in the City Via Del Monte has the highest number of persons who registered... followed by
PVDN and PVDW. Stickers are also available at the front counter.

13.  City Treasurer's Report - Status of City's Investments and the Current Investment
  Climate

Sherwood- Started with a refresher regarding our Investment Policy. We cannot invest in product
where we lose prinicpal or capital amounts, which limits us in what we can invest in but keeps the
City safe as far as Capital is concerned. As a result, we are limited to U.S. Treasuries, Federal
notes which we primarily have, and FDIC because we are insured by FDIC for up to $250,00. We
have to assume that none of these entities will go "belly up." The Fed would have to fail for us to
lose our principal. We do not expect to government to fail so we are safe with the investments we
have.

We also received a written report on, May 4, 2012, regarding the Municipal Treasurer's Meeting
that was held in Sacarmento. At the meeting state budgets and projections were presented...

Are we still $ 7 millon reserved. At years end. Paid off our PERS and paid off our capital LAIF
3.5%- SAFE SITTING THERE. Managed by the city treasurer. 2009 10 percentage that how them
Target has gone. 1.7 % 1.2 percent

Most economist expect these rates. All invest has a matuaryity date.Look at the rates every day. We
are hoping to 1.5%. The custodian is... Another question... am I going to continue working with the
